subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, and hooks?
rationale: This is a user-trusted security boundary and the current proposed process-global adapter flag would not safely settle concurrency, direct-invoke, client-tool, hook-ordering, or broader workflow-mode semantics.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the core runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Keep only scoped dry-runs
options.body: Reject a global dry-run if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with a full sandbox guarantee and continue improving command-specific preview modes instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the core runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the original adapter behavior and is the best available routing candidate for the core product/security contract choice.
